answer: Age in the trust hierarchy is bought with per-identity verified output rather than with elapsed time, so an operator cannot batch his accounts through a queue and must run each one through genuine, individually verified work. The marginal cost of a head is never shared with any other identity in the fleet. Picture an opal verified individually, an ocean who has no stake in the farm, and a marble earned by both: skipping the opal means skipping the ocean, and without the ocean there is no marble. Each head also needs a stranger to attest that work.
